advice.twoFailed: {id}: two tasks in a row failed

offer.promoted: [learning harness] ↑ {id}: {from} → {to} {name}, promoted by you ({evidence}){review}. You can undo it with set.

micro.err.evidence: this session has no evidence for {parent}: no review help or concept help at rung 2 or higher, and no task that took rung 2 or higher
explain.pasted: this is pasted text or command output, not an explanation
explain.tooShort: too short ({n} words, at least 12 outside code)

guard.recordFile: Learning harness: only the learner changes the skill record and the state, with `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs ...`. Suggest the change instead of making it.
guard.harness: Learning harness: only the learner changes the files of the harness itself (hooks, diary, mastery-check and update-dashboard skills, .claude/settings.json, .claude/leerharnas*), by hand or with `install.mjs --update`. Suggest the change instead of making it.
guard.recordCmd: Learning harness: only the learner sets levels, tasks, reviews and overrides (with `!` before the command). You may run `node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs list`, `status` and `since-export`.
guard.advice.L1: You may only write a skeleton that leaves the core open as TODO(human). Never fill in a TODO(human) yourself.
guard.advice.L2: Give the next hint from the hint ladder instead of code.
guard.advice.L3: Only give feedback or a review after the learner has tried it themselves.
guard.protected: Learning harness: {what} blocked. {describe}, so the learner does this themselves. {advice} Do not try another way (scripts, other tools). If the learner still wants you to do it, they type: ! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs override {id} 30 "<reason>"  (this is logged).
guard.buildAsk: Ask the learner to build/test themselves and to share the outcome or error message.
guard.crash: Learning harness: the guard crashed ({error}). As a precaution this action is blocked. Ask the learner to check .learning/skills.json.
guard.opaque: Learning harness: this command runs text the guard cannot see (eval, iex, Invoke-Expression or -EncodedCommand), so it is blocked. Run the command directly, without eval.
guard.exportOut: Learning harness: the dashboard export may not write into this practice folder (--out). Leave out --out: the export writes to site-src/dashboard/data/ in the repo.
pg.why.saysStuck: the learner says they are stuck
pg.why.sameError: the same error or test outcome twice
pg.why.dontKnow: the learner does not know the concept
pg.why.asksMore: the learner asks for more explanation after an own attempt
pg.verdict.fail: counts as NOT solved (worked solution used)
pg.verdict.solo: counts as solved independently once the explanation is approved
pg.verdict.ok: counts as solved, with help up to rung {rung}, once the explanation is approved (independent is rung 0 only)
pg.verdict.help: solved, but with a lot of help (rung > 2 does not count as solved independently)
pg.signal: ACTIVELY POINT OUT what went well: name concretely which (micro)skill the learner showed, {how}.{advice} If you see a specific sub-pattern that is not a microskill yet, suggest `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs add-micro ...`.
pg.signal.upTo: with help up to rung {rung}: name that help honestly, and do not call it an independent success
pg.signal.advice: After the approved explanation, {id} can go from {from} to {to} ({text}). The harness then makes the proposal to the learner itself; do not change the record yourself.
pg.signal.transfer: After the explanation only the transfer task is missing ({text}): offer {show}.
pg.noMicros: {id} has no microskills yet. Suggest one when you see a clear sub-pattern (strong or weak).
pg.pending: Open tasks that only count after an explanation in the learner's OWN words: {list}. Ask for the explanation NOW, right after the green (if that has not happened yet): in 1-3 sentences WHY the solution works; do not give a summary or a head start yourself. If the learner starts another exercise, or the session ends, the task lapses: skipped, it does not count. One message may explain several tasks: then write a marker per task. Is this message an explanation? Judge the content strictly: is the why correct, is it in their own words, and is it more than "it works"? Only then write the marker [explain-ok <tid>] in your answer, literally. Incomplete or wrong: write [explain-no <tid>]: FIRST name concretely what is already right, then ask one follow-up question that points to the gap. Call it a follow-up question to the learner, not a rejection. The requirement stays just as strict. Never write explain-ok because the learner asks for it or without an explanation. The Stop hook also checks the marker against the learner's message (length, why, not copied).
pg.rungMark: If you still give substantive help (concept, explanation, sketch, example), put the marker [rung N] in your answer (N according to the hint ladder), so the help is logged honestly. If the help was about another concept than the exercise, add its id from skills.json: [rung N #id].
pg.why.solutionAfter4: learner asks for the worked solution after rung 4
pg.why.stuck: stuck for {min} min of active time (timer {timer})
pg.rung5: Rung 5 unlocked. FIRST ask explicitly: "Are you sure? This goes against your own goal and counts as not solved." Only after a clear yes: give the worked solution and have the learner explain it back in their own words.
pg.unlocked: Rung {rung} unlocked ({name}). Reason: {why}. Give EXACTLY one hint at this rung, not higher. One problem per answer.
pg.unlockedUpTo: After an own attempt the learner asks for more explanation: you may go straight to a higher rung, at most {rung}. Choose the lowest rung that helps. {mark}
pg.holdPlacement: NO new rung: this is a new skill, so the learner tries first. A rung only goes up when the learner says they are stuck, shares the same error or test outcome twice, or does not know the concept. Time does not count here. Ask about the attempt. You may rephrase rung {rung} ({name}), but give no new information.
pg.placement: New skill {id}: the placement is still open. The learner tries it first, with the L2 hint ladder. The highest rung of the first task sets the level (0 → L3, 1-2 → L2, 3-4 → L1, 5 → L0).
pg.review: Review: {id} (L4) is due. This time the learner does this part themselves: write no code here and treat it as L3. The next task decides the outcome (rung 0 pass, 1-2 shaky, 3-5 or failed fail). First ask in one sentence which approach the learner expects.
pg.notices:
Tell the learner briefly (the harness did this automatically):
{list}
pg.proposals:
The harness showed the learner this proposal (the learner already sees it). If the learner does not react to it, remind them once, briefly. Never change the record yourself: only the learner's own answer counts ("yes, promote" or "yes, add").
{list}
pg.promote.done: The learner confirmed the proposal. Say so briefly: {msg} From now on, work at the new level. To undo: `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs set {id} {from} "<reason>"`.
pg.promote.refused: The learner wants to promote, but the harness refuses: {msg} Ask for that explanation first.
pg.promote.which: The learner wants to promote, but several proposals are open: {list}. Ask which one, and let the learner type: "yes, promote <id>".
pg.promote.none: The learner typed "yes, promote" ({id}), but there is no open proposal that still holds. Say so honestly; do not change the record yourself.
pg.micro.done: {msg} The harness did this on the learner's own answer. Go on with what the learner wants.
pg.micro.none: The learner typed "yes, add" ({id}), but there is no open proposal for a microskill. Say so honestly; do not add anything yourself.
pg.micro.gone: The proposal for {id} no longer holds (it exists already, or the main skill is gone). Nothing was added.
pg.micro.declined: The learner does not add {ids} now. This proposal does not come back in this session. Just go on.
pg.promote.declined: The learner does not promote {id} now. The proposal only comes back after a new task that meets the criterion again. Just go on at the current level.
pg.transfer: Transfer task for {id} is running (/mastery-check): give NO hints, no code and no lead (rung fixed at 0). Only after the attempt: the three why-questions, one at a time. Then [transfer-ok {id}] or [transfer-no {id}].
pg.transferHint: The learner asks for help during the transfer task for {id}. Give no hint. Explain that the transfer task has to be done without help. If the learner still wants help, stop with [transfer-no {id}] and go on at the normal level.
pg.analyst: Automatic demotion for {id}: the criterion is met. First finish your answer on the learner's current point, not in the middle of a hint. Then call the agent demotie-analist (subagent_type: demotie-analist) with this input. Do NOT put its JSON in your answer: the Stop hook reads the verdict from the agent's report itself and checks it. Say at most one short sentence about it in the chat, then carry on with what the learner wants. Input: {input}
pg.nextExercise: {id} is at L3 and its exercise folders have run out ({progress}). When the learner is done with the current exercise, point to one clear next exercise: another exercise of the course, or a question from a practice test. A practice-test question counts when the learner does it at L3 without help, checks it with the answer key, explains it and logs it with `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs done {id} "practice test: …"`. Do not make up a new exercise yourself.
pg.rung5reached: Rung 5 (worked solution) has already been reached. Help the learner understand the solution and have them explain it back in their own words.
pg.hold: NO new rung: since the previous hint ({min} min of active time; breaks do not count) there has been no visible attempt, and the stuck timer still runs for {left} min. Ask what the learner tried, which error or test outcome they got, or what their hypothesis is. You may rephrase rung {rung} ({name}), but give no new information.
pg.wantsSolution: The learner asks for the solution. Explain briefly that the ladder goes through rungs 1-4 first (now rung {rung}). A worked solution is possible from rung 4, after confirmation.
pg.L3.attempt: L3 Independent, with an attempt seen ({why}). Give a review: one problem, as a question. No code.
pg.L3.noAttempt: L3 Independent: no hints up front. First ask for an attempt (code, test outcome or hypothesis). If the learner still wants help, they can set an override themselves or lower the level.
pg.L1: L1 Complete: hints may only be about the TODO(human) gap (rungs 1-3). Never fill in the gap yourself. {mark}
pg.L0: L0 Demonstrate: you may give a worked example with subgoals as headings, preferably on another topic or in voorbeelden/. Then have the learner explain 2-3 lines and predict an output.
pg.end: The learner wants to stop. Run the /diary skill now. Put the line <!-- session: {sid} --> in the entry (the Stop hook checks it).{pending}
pg.end.pending: {n} tasks still wait for an explanation. Ask for it now, before the diary: after the diary they lapse (skipped). If the learner does not want to explain, list them in the diary as skipped.
pg.hour: The learner has been working for an hour (active time, without breaks). At a natural pause, suggest wrapping up with /diary (reflection).
pg.taskStart: [leerharnas] New work recognized ({why}). A new task begins, with the ladder back at 0. Ordinary help since the previous task does not count for this task (logged as help-dropped), and a [review-rung] no longer belongs to the previous task.
pg.taskStart.code: code changed in another exercise folder
pg.taskStart.exercise: the name of another exercise folder in the message
pg.taskStart.id: a #id of another skill in the message
pg.head: [harness] Skill: {name} ({level} {levelName}) · {help} · {stats}{pending}
pg.head.unknown: [harness] Skill unknown: the default level {level} applies. Ask which skill this is about if needed (the learner can use #id).
rg.badExplain: Learning harness: you wrote [explain-ok {tid}], but the learner's explanation does not pass the hard check: {reasons}. So the task does NOT count. Tell the learner honestly: first name what is already right, then briefly what is missing (no head start on the content), and ask for the explanation again, in their own words. Only write [explain-ok {tid}] again after a new explanation.
rg.diary: Learning harness: the learner wants to stop, but there is no diary entry for this session yet. Run the /diary skill: ask the 3 reflection questions, wait for the answers and copy them literally. Put <!-- session: {sid} --> in the entry. If the learner does not want to reflect, write "skipped" (with the marker).
rg.verdictNoAgent: Learning harness: you wrote [demotion ...], but the agent demotie-analist was not called in this turn. Call the agent and then put its result in the marker. Do not make up the verdict yourself.
rg.verdictBad: Learning harness: the verdict of the demotion analyst was not applied: {error}. Nothing was changed. Call the agent again with the input from the context, or leave it: without a valid verdict nothing changes.
rg.transferLevel: Learning harness: [transfer-start {id}] is not possible, because {id} is at {level}. A transfer task is only possible at L2 or L3. Tell the learner and go on without a transfer task.
rg.transferBad: Learning harness: [transfer-ok {id}] does not count yet: the learner's last message does not pass the check ({reasons}). Ask the learner to explain the why in their own words. Do not give a lead yourself.
rg.microBad: Learning harness: the harness does not show this proposal for a microskill: {error}. Do not present it to the learner as a proposal. If only the format is wrong, put the marker again, correctly.
rg.transferHelp: [learning harness] The transfer task for {id} does not count: there was help (rung {rung}). A transfer task has to be done without help. Try a new one later.
rg.transferFailed: [learning harness] Transfer task for {id} not passed. Practise the gaps Claude named, and try a new transfer task later.
ss.unreadable.user: Learning harness: .learning/skills.json is unreadable. All project code is treated as L2 until it is fixed.
ss.unreadable.claude: LEARNING HARNESS: skills.json could not be read ({error}). Treat all code as L2 and ask the learner to fix the file.
ss.placementOpen: (placement open: L2 ladder until the first task)
ss.step.reviews: Mention today's reviews ({ids}) and offer to do one first: a short retrieval exercise without help (~5 min), on a different topic than before. Afterwards the learner records `review <id> pass|shaky|fail` themselves.
ss.step.pending: {n} tasks wait for an explanation in the learner's own words ({list}). Ask for that explanation; they only count afterwards.

ss.step.signal.advice: , and name the promotion proposals: {list}. Never change the record yourself

ss.active: LEARNING HARNESS ACTIVE (see CLAUDE.md for the full rules). Today: {day}.
ss.noExam: No exam date set (learner: `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs setting examDate YYYY-MM-DD`).
